posts.content:
Across stages, Accenture Song’s conversations at Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity revolved around how businesses can stay relevant, drive growth and turn creative ideas into real impact. 

1. Ndidiamaka Oteh joined Variety x Canva to discuss why leaders are doubling down on AI to unlock both creativity and more personal, connected experiences. 
2. Hiroyuki Yokoi explored what the world could look like 18 months from now—cutting through what’s hype, what’s lasting and what leaders should be preparing for next. 
3. Mia Rafowitz unpacked the reality behind creative endurance, sharing the G.R.I.T. factor and what it takes for talent to stay, grow and succeed in high-pressure environments. 
4. Damon Stapleton took us inside the Industry Craft Lions jury room, revealing what set this year’s winning work apart and where the bar for creative excellence is being set. 
5. Stephanie Sadowski joined leaders from Salesforce and The Drum to explore what it takes to lead in the agentic era—and why the next generation of CMOs will need a fundamentally different model. 
6. Rajat Agarwal discussed how agentic commerce is transforming discovery, trust and conversion, and what it means for how brands show up across the path to purchase. 
7. Reema R. Sanghvi explored how companies are turning signals into action—building the data and AI foundations teams need to move faster and make smarter decisions. 
8. Ami Palan  discussed brand trust and consumer expectations in the age of AI at Brand Innovators Beach. 
9 and 10. Ndidi Oteh and Nick Law took to the Lumière Theatre stage to discuss Applied Creativity, why creative leadership belongs in the C-suite, and the commitment, structure and expertise that turn imagination into meaningful products and experiences.  

We had a great time at #CannesLions2026! 🦁 

Explore more from Cannes and our latest thinking here: https://accntu.re/4bh215e  

[Image description: Gallery of pictures of our leaders during Cannes Lions 2026.]

posts.content:
We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dame Annette King. One of the industry’s fiercest and brightest stars, and previously our global marketing practice lead.  

A message from David Droga: 

This week we lost our friend, colleague and co-conspirator, Dame Annette King.  

Even writing that feels strange. Some people leave a mark on a company. Annette left a mark on the people inside it. 

Annette carried that rare mix of sharp intelligence, generosity, curiosity, and a wonderfully dry sense of humor that could quietly recalibrate or rehabilitate a room. She made things clearer. Calmer. Better. It was a genuine privilege to work alongside her. And if I am honest, it was also good old-fashioned fun. She took the role and responsibility very seriously, but never herself. Annette had a way of cutting through noise without cutting down people. She was thoughtful without being solemn, authoritative without ever being self-important, and always deeply human. 

Across our industry she was admired from many vantage points not only for what she achieved, but for how she achieved it. She helped shape brands, businesses, and careers, but more importantly she helped shape confidence in others. She also had that rare ability to be appropriately tough while being seismically kind and considerate at the same time. 

Today our thoughts are with her husband Henry, her beloved children Carter and Sylvie, and the many people around the world who loved and admired her and had the privilege of knowing her privately or professionally. Loss like this reminds us that the real architecture of any company is the people inside it. Annette strengthened those foundations wherever she went.  

Annette will be deeply missed. But the wisdom, warmth, and standards she brought into our orbit will remain with many of us for a long time. 

Don't forget to hug the people you love more often than you think you should. (And ignore those who tax your soul.) Life is too short. 

With sadness and gratitude, 

David 

[Image Description: Professional portrait of a woman in a black blazer and white collared shirt with a delicate necklace. She has shoulder-length wavy golden-brown hair and a confident, approachable expression. The background features a modern office interior with gray walls and neutral architectural elements.]

🌊 Every year, 75,000 km of ghost nets are lost to our oceans, killing hundreds of thousands of marine animals. Finding them has been the hard part; until now.
 
Sonar data that could locate ghost nets already exists, buried in archives from pipeline surveys, research expeditions, naval scans. Reviewing it manually takes too long. So, we partnered with WWF Deutschland and Microsoft's AI for Good Lab to reframe the problem: not a funding gap, but a data-sharing one.
 
GhostNetZero turns existing sonar into recovery coordinates. 95% detection accuracy. Red Dot Design Award: Best of the Best.
 
The most impactful solutions don't always demand new technology. They demand we connect what we already have. 
 
Read the full story: https://accntu.re/408o9sH

How do you sell a material that transforms invisible light into heat? 🌞

Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd. faced exactly that with SOLAMENT™ : a near-infrared absorbing material with real applications, but no way for people to grasp what it actually does.
 
Droga5, part of Accenture Song, made one move: build a jacket that proves it. No down insulation. Just sunlight converted to heat. One tangible prototype that answered every question the tech specs couldn't.
 
The result: 500% lead growth and multiple Red Dot Design Award, including Best of the Best.  Industries from agriculture to outdoor gear asking the same question: if it works there, what about here? 

Sometimes you don't need to explain innovation. You need to let people experience it: https://accntu.re/4q5UxH9

[Image Description: Translucent quilted jacket featuring SOLAMENT™ technology that converts light to heat. Lifestyle and product shots with purple Accenture Song branding and text about innovation and prototype impact.]

Did you know more than 1 million tons of plastic enter Indonesia’s oceans each year?

Project STOP, co-founded by Borealis  and Systemiq Ltd.  in partnership with the Indonesian government—is tackling this challenge by helping establish sustainable, circular waste management systems that protect the environment and create green jobs.

Together, we developed the Project STOP Banyuwangi Hijau App, a digital solution designed for low-connectivity areas that’s transforming how waste is collected and tracked. The app has already reached nearly 30,000 households, with plans to expand to 377,000, helping stop waste leakage at its source and connecting more communities to formal waste management systems.

Read more about how we’re combining technology, creativity, and human-centered design to turn the tide on plastic pollution: https://accntu.re/3LtuWJB

[Video description: The video begins with Ayu standing in a green rice field in Banyuwangi, Indonesia, introducing herself. It cuts between shots of her walking through the fields and aerial views of terraced farmland and palm trees. This is followed by images of unmanaged waste — burning trash, rivers filled with debris, and garbage piles — showing local waste challenges.

Ayu then introduces Project STOP. Footage shows a waste collector loading bins into a yellow and green vehicle, a video call with a partner from Borealis, and community members writing on large sheets of paper. At a recycling facility, workers in safety gear sort plastic waste.

Door-to-door collection is shown, along with a smartphone app that registers households, tracks pickups, and logs payments. The app interface appears on screen, integrated with scenes of workers using it in neighborhoods.

The final scenes return to Ayu, now on a beach, standing near collected waste. On-screen graphics show over 56,000 tons of waste collected and more than 350,000 people reached. The video ends with a wide shot of Ayu near the word "STOP" spelled out in trash and a logo for Project STOP, and co-founders Borealis and Systemiq]

Customer service is broken. And your customers know it. 😐 They’re tired of waiting. Tired of repeating themselves. Tired of wondering why a brand that knows everything about them still can’t get it right.
 
The result? 87% will leave after just one bad experience.
 
Fixing this isn’t just about better tech or faster response times. It’s about rethinking customer service from the ground up—because what worked yesterday won’t cut it tomorrow.
 
New regulations, like the Keep Call Centers in America Act 2025, are raising the bar on transparency, agent location, and responsible AI use. The future of service demands more than efficiency—it demands integrity, intelligence, and human connection.
 
Our latest report outlines three key actions to drive transformation:
- Personalize every interaction to build trust.
- Predict and proactively address customer needs.
- Foster collaboration by placing service at the core.
 
Forget faster chatbots. Start making smarter, enterprise-wide decisions. When you unlock the full potential of AI and Machine Enablement, customer service doesn’t just improve, it becomes a growth engine.
 
Read our report to learn how to turn customer service into a Customer Growth Engine: https://accntu.re/4qkmrAt
